prompt: Close-up of the whole chilled Spekulatius-Tiramisu for four, uncut in its small transparent rectangular 20 × 15 cm glass dish. Two thick layers of smooth, softly set ivory quark–mascarpone cream dominate, with faint cinnamon warmth and tiny orange-zest flecks. Between them sits a thinner, juicy layer of thawed deep-ruby raspberries, their soft whole and slightly collapsed shapes held in a little red syrup that lightly stains the adjoining cream. Thin rectangular spice-brown biscuits form the bottom and middle layers, now tender and cake-like from chilling, visible through the glass rather than crisp. The upper cream is smoothly spread with subtle spatula marks and a fine matte cocoa–cinnamon dusting surrounding a sharply defined, undusted pale star left by the lifted stencil. A restrained optional garnish of red raspberries and small fresh mint leaves rests at one corner without obscuring the pattern. The generously filled dish nearly reaches the edges of the square frame. Photographed at about 65 degrees so both the patterned top and distinct side layers are clear, in bright soft natural daylight with crisp detail and true-to-life colours. Pale warm wood and a narrow edge of natural linen create a calm, clean, unmarked background.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 200 g frozen raspberries total, 50 g per serving, mixed with 1 packet vanilla sugar total, 0.25 packet per serving; all form one substantially thinner middle layer beneath the dominant cream quantity.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: After mixing and prolonged chilling, the berries are thawed rather than frosty or cooked: deep ruby red, glossy and juicy, with some plump whole berry shapes and others slightly collapsed. A little red juice and syrup moistens their layer and lightly stains the adjacent cream; the vanilla sugar is no longer separately visible.

visible_ingredients.name_de: Quark–Mascarpone-Creme mit Puderzucker, Orangensaft, Orangenschale und Zimt
visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 375 g Magerquark and 375 g mascarpone total, each 93.75 g per serving, with 100 g icing sugar total, 25 g per serving, 2 EL orange juice total, 0.5 EL per serving, 0.5 TL finely grated organic orange zest total, 0.125 TL per serving, and the 1 Msp cinnamon specified in step 1. Together these provide most of the dessert's volume, divided into two cream layers; the supplied cinnamon value of 999–999 is not a usable quantity.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: A homogeneous, smooth and very creamy pale-ivory mixture, softly firmer after chilling but still supple rather than rubbery. It holds spatula marks and clean layer edges; minute orange-zest flecks may be visible, while the juice, icing sugar and cinnamon are fully incorporated, with no separate orange sauce.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 10 biscuits total, 2.5 per serving, distributed between the base and central layers specified in step 2; they remain much less voluminous than the cream.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Thin, rectangular, spice-brown biscuits with darker baked edges. Their visible side edges are softened and tender, almost cake-like where they have absorbed moisture during chilling, not hard or crisp; their embossed faces are largely concealed within the layers.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 1.5 TL cocoa powder total, 0.375 TL per serving, mixed in step 3 with 0.5 TL cinnamon for a light surface dusting.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: A fine, dry, matte warm-brown veil over the exposed top cream, leaving a clearly defined pale star where the lifted cardboard star masked the surface. The dusting is thin enough to retain the cream's smooth texture.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: Optional according to taste, with no additional quantity supplied; if shown, kept as a very small corner garnish so the central raspberry layer remains the principal fruit presence.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Small fresh green mint leaves with natural soft surfaces and a few glossy red raspberries, used sparingly without covering the star pattern.

recipe_result: A chilled, softly set Spekulatius-Tiramisu for four, shown whole and uncut in its 20 × 15 cm family-style dish, with two softened spiced-biscuit layers, two generous quark–mascarpone cream layers, a juicy raspberry middle layer, and a cocoa–cinnamon top patterned by a star stencil.
ingredient_context: TK-Himbeeren: 200 g total; 50 g per serving; Vanillezucker: 1 Packung total; 0.25 Packung per serving; Magerquark: 375 g total; 93.75 g per serving; Puderzucker: 100 g total; 25 g per serving; Zimt: 999–999 total; per-serving quantity unavailable; Mascarpone: 375 g total; 93.75 g per serving; Orangensaft: 2 EL total; 0.5 EL per serving; fein abgeriebene Schale einer Bio-Orange: 0.5 TL total; 0.125 TL per serving; Spekulatius-Kekse: 10 Ungültige Einheit total; 2.5 Ungültige Einheit per serving; Kakaopulver: 1.5 TL total; 0.375 TL per serving
final_plating_from_recipe: Step 2 builds the dessert in a roughly 20 × 15 cm dish in this exact order: biscuit base, half the quark cream, all the raspberry mixture, a second biscuit layer, then the remaining cream, followed by at least five hours of chilling. Step 3 finishes the chilled top with cocoa mixed with cinnamon around the star mask, then removes the mask; optional mint leaves and raspberries are added only at serving. Show the complete family-style dessert, preferably in a clear rectangular glass dish that reveals the side layers, with no serving removed.

recipe_instructions.instruction: Gefrorene Himbeeren mit Vanillezucker mischen. Magerquark mit Puderzucker und 1 Msp. Zimt in ca. 5 Min. sehr cremig rühren. Mascarpone mit Orangensaft und Bio-Orangenschale glatt rühren, vorsichtig unter die Quarkmasse rühren.

Eine Form (ca. 20 x 15 cm) mit 5–6 Spekulatius-Keksen auslegen. Hälfte der Quarkcreme daraufstreichen. Himbeeren darauf verteilen. Mit weiteren 5–6 Spekulatius-Keksen belegen. Die übrige Creme darauf verteilen. Tiramisu mindestens 5 Std., besser über Nacht, kalt stellen.

Aus Pappe einen Stern ausschneiden. Schablone auf das Spekulatius-Tiramisu legen. 1/2 TL Zimt mit Kakao mischen und das Tiramisu damit bestäuben. Stern-Schablone vorsichtig wieder abheben. Spekulatius-Tiramisu nach Geschmack mit Minz- blättern und Himbeeren servieren.
